description: The pie chart represents the distribution of emotional states in a study on speaker anonymization. There are six categories depicted: Frustration, Neutral, Happiness, Sadness, Anger, and a category that is not labeled in the image. Frustration accounts for the largest portion at 25.1%, followed by Neutral at 23.1%, and Happiness at 8.1%. Anger and Sadness are relatively close, with Anger at 14.9% and Sadness at 14.7%, while the unlabeled category is slightly lower at 14.1%. The chart includes percentage labels inside each slice, and the colors are distinguishable, with Frustration in blue, Neutral in purple, Happiness in red, Anger in yellow, Sadness in orange, and the unlabeled category in green. There is no legend, and no slices are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and percentage labels. The segments are ordered by size, with Frustration being the largest and Happiness the smallest.
